pr_title: usockets: back off a listener whose accept() fails instead of spinning the event loop
pr_body:
### Problem
- When `accept()` fails and leaves the connection queued (for example `EMFILE`), the event loop spins. Released 1.4.3 makes 197,390 failed `accept4` calls per second.
- The cause is the empty failure arm in `us_internal_dispatch_ready_poll` (`packages/bun-usockets/src/loop.c`), marked `/* Todo: start timer here */`.

### Fix
- On epoll and kqueue, `us_internal_accept_back_off` takes the listener out of the poll set. The loop registers it again 5 ms later. The connection stays in the backlog.
- The retry reuses `sweep_next_tick_ns`, the deadline that the loop already turns into its poll timeout.
- Correct because nothing retries `accept()` with no delay. The tick and a successful accept keep their instruction counts.
- Verified: new tests in `test/js/bun/http/serve-syscall-fault.test.ts`, `test/js/bun/net/socket-syscall-fault.test.ts` and `test/js/node/net/net-syscall-fault.test.ts` fail without the change.

### Background
- A level-triggered poll reports a listener readable for as long as a connection is queued.
- The sweep deadline normally fires every 4 s to expire idle sockets.
- Designs weighed: a reserve descriptor that accepts and closes queued connections resets clients that bun serves today. A pause until the 4 s sweep starves a busy server.

### Downsides
- A server at its descriptor limit pauses 5 ms after each failed `accept()`. Debug builds, 64 clients, median requests/s of 6 rounds: 62 against 172 with 1 free descriptor, 141 against 271 with 2, 236 against 257 with 8.
- While the failure lasts, the loop makes 158 failed `accept4` and 317 `epoll_ctl` calls per second.
- +605 bytes of code. Windows is not changed: the libuv backend keeps the old behaviour. No machine ran the kqueue arm.
extra_context: Design picked before the code was written: listener-backoff-deadline, because every listener API reaches accept() through two call sites in one function (loop.c), and the in-branch placement with one sweep reference per episode measured +0 instructions on tick, accept and link. A fixed 5 ms retry is the only measured schedule that keeps a server at its fd limit serving, and it matches the contract of the maintainer's open #42819. Why not the minimal patch: a pause whose only re-arm is the 4 s sweep fills the same branch at the same +0 cost, but a server at its limit then accepts once per 4 s and recovery takes 0 to 4 s. Origin: a request in team chat from a Bun team member. A syscall fault injector found that Bun.serve spins at 100% CPU when accept4 returns EMFILE. No GitHub issue exists. This diff replaces the current head of PR oven-sh/bun#32705 (402e15cba2: a reserve descriptor per loop, an accept-and-close drain, a stderr warning, a 200 ms pause), which a review on 2026-10-01 criticized. Rule explicitly on one decision: this diff is POSIX only. The design's plan had a libuv (Windows) arm: park the listener with us_poll_change(p, loop, 0) and restore it from a lazy one-shot 5 ms us_timer. It was written and then dropped because nothing could run it (no Windows machine, the fault-injection tests run on ASAN Linux builds only), the spin was never observed on Windows, and maintainer PR #42819 (Remove libuv on Windows) deletes eventing/libuv.c and internal/eventing/libuv.h, which that arm edited. So the call in the accept branch is under #ifndef LIBUS_USE_LIBUV, and accept_backoff_sweep_ns is unconditional in loop_data.h and InternalLoopData.rs so that the Rust mirror stays right when #42819 removes the cfg(windows) split. Is that the right cut, or must the libuv arm come back? An earlier review run of the version with the libuv arm lost its verdict to a machine reset. Measurements for this change (Linux x64, debug + ASAN builds of the PR and of the same base): 10 s at a real descriptor limit with one queued client: PR 1,584 failed accept4 and 3,173 epoll_ctl, base 245,908 failed accept4. Objects compiled with the release flags, ThinLTO off: us_internal_sweep_if_due has 3 instructions with the sweep off and 18 when armed and not due on both sides, a successful accept has the same instruction sequence, .text grows by 605 bytes. The tests in the three syscall-fault files passed on a debug + ASAN build before the libuv arm was dropped. The test 'accept → ECONNABORTED or EPROTO' in net-syscall-fault.test.ts is new and has not run yet.
open_prs: #42819 by dylan-conway, 'Remove libuv on Windows' (open, not draft, 469 files): deletes packages/bun-usockets/src/eventing/libuv.c and internal/eventing/libuv.h and changes the accept call in loop.c. #39641 and #44455 touch the failure path of loop creation (not verified here).
linked: No GitHub issue. Origin: a team chat request after a syscall fault injector run. Repro: Bun.serve under a low `ulimit -n`, all descriptors taken, one client queued. Released 1.4.3-canary.1 (367d939d9) then makes 137,000 to 197,000 failed accept4 calls per second until a descriptor is free.
env_preamble: The change under review is the head of branch farm/36c27092/usockets-accept-emfile-backoff in /workspace/bun. If packages/bun-usockets/src/loop.c has no us_internal_accept_back_off, the container was reset: run `git fetch origin farm/36c27092/accept-backoff-wip` and read files with `git show FETCH_HEAD:<path>`. Do not start `bun bd`, cargo or ninja: a build may be running in /workspace/bun/build/debug, and two builds in one directory break each other. When /workspace/bun/build/debug/bun-debug is newer than 2026-10-03 02:00 UTC it is a debug + ASAN build of this change: run it directly. /workspace/bun/build/release/bun is released 1.4.3-canary.1 without the change. Kill every process you start before you finish: orphaned children keep running and starve the container.
